clue.text: What makes rich VIP cry? Conservative gain with pain

indicators.note: the question asks what the letters of these words can be made into, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political question: what would make a rich celebrity weep, and the reply is a Tory win bought at great cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What makes' gives PYRRHICVIC from the jumbled letters; the surface's political win is the definition in disguise, a victory won at ruinous cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pyrrhic victory is a win so costly that it is hardly worth having, named after King Pyrrhus of Epirus.

clue.text: Exhibitor at the Walker Gallery?

parts.note: the Walker is a real Liverpool art gallery, but read it as a gallery for walkers: a street artist chalks pictures on the footway for passers-by

explanation.surface: Someone showing paintings at Liverpool's Walker Art Gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Walker Art Gallery is in Liverpool; here the 'gallery' is the pedestrian's footway, where chalk pictures are drawn for passing walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A street artist who chalks pictures on the footway displays work to those walking past, a gallery for walkers.

clue.text: Lawrence's work with artist from the East End

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword abbreviation for an artist
someone from the East End of London might live in Bow, one of its districts

explanation.surface: A D.H. Lawrence novel paired with a painter from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of the East End of London, so a person from there is 'in Bow'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rainbow is a 1915 novel by D.H. Lawrence, so it is one of the writer's works.

clue.text: Death's one sad memento mori

indicators.note: sad in the sense of sorry or poor in state, so these letters are put in a sorry jumble

parts.note: the possessive is read as the plain letters of the word with its s

explanation.surface: Death's single gloomy reminder of mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad' rearranges DEATHS into HEADST, the apostrophe ignored as crosswords allow; ONE stays as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave marker is a classic reminder of mortality, which is what the Latin phrase memento mori means.

clue.text: Chief of Men caught by memory, successfully

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ROM is read-only memory in computing
well means successfully, as in did well

explanation.surface: A leader of men trapped by his own memory, but doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's sonnet to the Lord Protector opens 'Cromwell, our chief of men', which supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's sonnet addresses the Lord Protector as 'our chief of men', so the phrase is a literary title for him.

clue.text: Getting close to the French eventually

definitions.meaning: the French word for intimate or close is spelt this way
sooner or later, given enough time

explanation.surface: Becoming friendly with the French, in due course.
explanation.definitionFit: The French adjective for intimate fits the first sense, and the English phrase meaning sooner or later fits the second.

clue.text: Prodigal Athenian: 'I'm putting on weight'

parts.note: T is short for ton, a unit of weight
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they are gaining a few pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue the pieces stack as weight, then I'M, then ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens is a wealthy Athenian who squanders his fortune on false friends, a prodigal.

clue.text: First person's first person?

parts.note: the first person of the realm, the monarch, has a first-person pronoun of their own, a plural used for one

explanation.surface: A grammar question about the first person singular.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'first person' is the monarch, the first in the land; the second is the grammatical first person, here the plural used by a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch speaking of themselves in the plural uses a first-person pronoun reserved for royalty.

clue.text: Its help for free for the one of you two, they say; hoi polloi get nothing

parts.words: for the one of you two, they say
parts.note: 'you two' sounds like U2, the band, whose singer is Bono; 'for' in Latin is pro, so 'for Bono'
hoi polloi are the general public

explanation.surface: Some puzzling advice about free assistance for a pair of people, while the masses go without.
explanation.walkthrough: PUBLIC (hoi polloi) gets O (nothing) at the end. The Latin phrase means 'for the public good', the sense of work done unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Work done for the public good is done without charge, so the Latin phrase describes free help.

clue.text: In France, that's all the fuel; see a solicitor about it!

parts.note: V is short for the Latin vide, meaning see
oil is a fuel
a tout solicits custom

explanation.surface: A French driver says that is all the petrol, and suggests seeing a lawyer about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits custom, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase translates as 'that's all', so it is what someone in France says for it.

clue.text: Livingstone returns as king, giving up 50 for 1,000

indicators.note: in Roman numerals 50 is L and 1,000 is M, so one letter is swapped for the other
returns means the word for kingly is read backwards

parts.note: royal describes acting as a king does

explanation.surface: Ken Livingstone makes a comeback like a monarch, exchanging small change for a big sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ROYAL into LAYOR; 'giving up 50 for 1,000' swaps its L for M. Ken Livingstone was the first Mayor of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Livingstone was the first elected Mayor of London, so his name stands for the office he held.

clue.text: Income Boswell derived from dried apricots

indicators.note: the answer is drawn straight out of the run of letters in the words before it

explanation.surface: Earnings that Boswell got from selling dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derived from' takes the letters inside 'incoME BOSwell'. Mebos is a South African confection.
explanation.definitionFit: Mebos is a South African sweetmeat made of salted or sugared dried apricots, so the fruit defines it.

clue.text: Masculine bowels in torment with this movement

indicators.note: torment twists and racks the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for masculine in grammar

explanation.surface: A man in gut-wrenching agony over a political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torment' rearranges M, BOWELS and IN; the feminist cause is fittingly made of a masculine piece in agony.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's liberation movement of the 1960s and 70s is commonly shortened to this phrase.

clue.text: Dvorak's work adding line to neologism

indicators.note: adding the line into the coined word places it inside

parts.note: a neologism is a newly coined word

explanation.surface: A Dvorak composition gains an extra line to become a fresh coinage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adding' puts L inside NEW WORD before its final D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dvorak's Ninth Symphony is known as 'From the New World', a famous orchestral work.

clue.text: Translator cut down in foreign news broadcast

indicators.note: in places the shortened translator inside the scrambled news
foreign suggests something strange or alien, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: TR is the shortened form of translator

explanation.surface: An interpreter is reduced to a minor part in a foreign news programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' gives SEWN from the scrambled news; 'broadcast' looks like the programme but means scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast in its old sense means scattered widely, like seed sown by hand, which matches scattered about.

clue.text: 'Time', Mad Margaret's four-letter word

indicators.note: mad suggests something deranged, so the name's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the name is read without its possessive s

explanation.surface: Mad Margaret, from Gilbert and Sullivan's Ruddigore, uses a rude word for 'time'.
explanation.walkthrough: Mad Margaret is a character in Gilbert and Sullivan's Ruddigore; 'Mad' rearranges MARGARET.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word of four letters, from Greek tetra, four, and gramma, letter.

clue.text: Somehow, using hot iron first gives sense of direction in China

indicators.note: first places the iron symbol at the front of the rest

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Using a hot iron first, someone mysteriously gains a sense of direction in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' gives NGSHUI from the jumbled letters. 'Sense of direction' plays on the orientation of buildings in Chinese geomancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Feng shui is the Chinese art of arranging buildings and rooms by orientation and flow of energy.

clue.text: Preventive medicine, when taken daily with tense application in Java

parts.note: an apple a day keeps the doctor away, as the proverb says
T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar

explanation.surface: A remedy taken every day, combined with a stressful app, on an Indonesian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Java' looks like the island but is the programming language.
explanation.definitionFit: An applet is a small program written in the Java language that runs inside another application.

clue.text: Spanish hotel for the Spanish includes a small heater

indicators.note: includes means the Spanish word wraps around the rest

parts.note: por is Spanish for for
rad is short for radiator

explanation.surface: A Spanish hotel, said to be for the locals, comes with a little radiator.
explanation.walkthrough: Spanish por, meaning for, wraps the other pieces. Paradors are a well-known chain of state hotels in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A parador is a state-run hotel in Spain, often set in a historic building.

clue.text: Train spotters in a Route 66 lay-by?

indicators.note: train means to direct or arrange, so the letters are lined up anew

explanation.surface: Railway enthusiasts are found at a lay-by on the famous American highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' rearranges SPOTTERS. A lay-by is the British term for a roadside parking area; Route 66 is an American highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest stop is the American term for a roadside place to pull over, the counterpart of a British lay-by.

clue.text: Twit, as it were, in rebellion

parts.note: the word is read as T plus wit, and wit, meaning reason, is replaced by that synonym

explanation.surface: Calling someone a fool is, so to speak, an act of revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it were' tells the solver to read 'Twit' as T followed by WIT, and WIT means reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country or sovereign, an act of rebellion against the state.

clue.text: Satellite carrying jolly prophet of Utah

indicators.note: carrying means the satellite holds the marine inside it

parts.note: the moon is Earth's satellite
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A satellite carries a cheerful prophet of Utah.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Mormon is the prophet who in Latter-day Saint belief compiled the Book of Mormon; the church is centred in Utah.

clue.text: 'Lover Come Back To Me' — a light air?

parts.note: a torch is a light
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: A classic love song is described as a gentle tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover Come Back To Me' is a 1928 Romberg and Hammerstein standard, a lament for lost love.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch song is a sentimental ballad of unrequited or lost love, and this standard is an example.

clue.text: Bird woman's refusal to return

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: to return means the refusal is turned to read backwards

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A woman's no is reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes.

clue.text: Cause célèbre cause of some back-biting!

indicators.note: back means the letters taken are read in reverse
of some takes a few letters from within the words before it

explanation.surface: A cause célèbre that started with malicious gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of some' takes BRECA from 'célèBRE CAuse', and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb means sharp or bitter in taste or manner, as biting remarks are.

clue.text: Feast of prophet taking daughter to heart

indicators.note: taking means the prophet holds something within
to heart says the item goes into the middle of the word

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: A prophet's feast where he lovingly embraces his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... to heart' puts D in the middle of SEER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seder is the ritual feast held on the first night or nights of Passover.

clue.text: Gandhi, rejecting TM and a version of his RI from this teacher

indicators.note: rejecting means the listed letters are thrown out of Gandhi's title

parts.note: Gandhi was known as Mahatma, great soul

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gandhi turns away from Transcendental Meditation and a version of his religious instruction, from this guru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' takes T, M and A out of MAHATMA, leaving MAHA; 'version of' rearranges HIS RI into RISHI. The teacher is the one behind TM.
explanation.definitionFit: Maharishi Mahesh Yogi was the Indian guru who taught Transcendental Meditation; maharishi means great sage.

clue.text: Murcian not open for negotiation with the Caudillo's edict?

indicators.note: open for negotiation means the terms can be rearranged, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A man from Murcia refuses to bargain over General Franco's decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for negotiation' rearranges MURCIAN NOT OPEN, a fair irony since a dictator's edict is not open to negotiation. The Caudillo was General Franco of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronunciamento is a manifesto or military proclamation in Spanish-speaking countries, apt for Franco.
